To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
orbital excitations of vector mesons are produced in DIS with a large probability at small Q 2.

orbital excitations are dominant at low Q 2, that the ratio of the cross sections for the production of the orbital and radial excitations is about 1:3, that the longitudinal cross section for orbital excitations is strongly suppressed, and that mixing between radial and D -wave excitations is small.
the diffractive production in DIS is dominated by the s -channel D -wave states and that the s -channel transitions contribute ∼50% to the longitudinal cross section.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the production of orbitally exited mesons in the small- x regime is very sensitive to the dynamics in the hard parton-parton scattering subprocess, and therefore can serve as a probe for the dynamics in hard parton-partonic scattering.

the k t -based approach is able to provide a unified description of the diffractive production cross sections of both radial and orbital excitates, and the predicted suppression of σ L / σ t is in a very good agreement with data.
